Quality Indian food at a very fair price
Feb 2018 • Couples
Have dined a Mumtaz on a previous visit. The restaurant is almost on the street, in a Vietnamese way. 

This is the best Indian restaurant, in terms of the food, in which I’ve dined in Saigon; I have dined in several over the years. The restaurant itself has little ambience, drawing its ambience from the frenetic Bui Viện St. If you want calm and quiet, go to District 1. There is significant competition, which brings the price down and the quality up. The service was very good and our waiter was genuinely friendly and informative. 
Recommended. BTW, we had just flown in, following a tour of Rajasthan, India so we’d had some world-class curries prior to our visiting Mumtaz.

Great Indian!
Nov 2017 • Friends
Ok, not gonna lie, I really didn’t have any expectations coming in. My husband and I live in Ho Chi Minh long term and pretty much only come into Bui Vien to show guests our exciting backpacker street once every blue moon. And we try not to eat there because locals think of Bui Vien as a tourist trap. Our friends invited us to join them for dinner at Mumtaz’s because they met him a while ago and he had invited them to check out his restaurant.

But WOW was the food ever amazing!!!!!! Our friends ordered a green cheese dish that was To. Die. For. I ordered my favorite,eggplant masala, and hubby ordered his favorite butter chicken. We also had some amazing appetizers, the butter and garlic naan was incredible. Sorry I don’t know the names of all the dishes, I’m usually not the one who orders when we go for Indian food so I’m not very well versed in dish names. 

Also, Mumtaz came out to talk to us and he’s absolutely adorable and so hospital!! He felt so bad because there wasn’t enough parking out front so we had to park two bikes across the street and they tried to charge us for it and he actually went out and paid the parking for us. 

The best part? No upset stomach issues after! We went home stuffed and happy and slept all night and woke up wanting more of last night’s amazing dinner! So now we’re actually going to have to pop into Bui Vien more often to go eat at Mumtaz’s!!

Firstly received a poppadum and a selection of three spices before I ordered my main, all free of charge the waitress explained.

Service was quick and the food was delicious! Succulent, good quality chicken breast and fantastic taste. 

I'd also ordered some garlic na'an which came with a vegetable curry sauce. 

The whole meal took a while to eat, so it was incredible satisfying, but I was slightly concerned about the price. I had realised the menu was quite expensive, and seeing as I'd ordered three seperate dishes, I suspected the bill to exceed my mental price barrier of 200,000d.

I got the check and alas, 183,000d. Perfect and worth every last Dong!
The service was great, with the girls being very friendly and helpful so I handed over the 200.000 bill and told them to keep the rest for themselves. Well deserved!

Dec 2014 • Couples
If I were rating it on the Saigon Indian food scale, I'd rate it five stars. On the world Indian food scale (US, UK, Malaysia, Thailand) it rates a solid three stars. So I'm averaging those out to give a four-star rating.

Other Pham Ngu Lao Indian restaurants set the bar pretty low. They're just plain bad. Mumtaz has good stuff. It's clear that they're a low-volume restaurant and don't really have many of the real Indian ingredients, nor probably even the real equipment (Tandoori oven)... but they still create some very good food. 

Other reviewers said the portions are big, but I think they're small, at least compared to US standards. Maybe ok for Asia standards, but even for Asian standards, I wouldn't call the portions big.

The Indian dudes running the place are great, and speak perfect English. Try to order from them, rather than from the waiter/waitress kids. The kids try hard, but don't really speak English, and don't know anything about Indian food, so there's a lot of risk for mistakes.

Delicious, Friendly, and Affordable
I've lived in Ho Chi Minh City for almost a year and in that time I've eaten a lot of pho. But sometimes I'm sick of soup and I want something more flavorful, and on these occasions I almost always head to Mumtaz. Mumtaz is without doubt the most tasty restaurant in the backpacker neighborhood (Pham Ngu Lao) as well as one of the best Indian restaurants in town. 

The food is fresh and delicious, and they offer both North and South Indian dishes prepared by specialist cooks. I'm a big fan of spicy Southern cooking--I love vindaloos--while my girlfriend prefers the creamier, more subtly flavored Northern dishes like paneer butter masala, and both of us are inevitably pleased. It's clear the kitchen really cares about the food, both its taste & presentation, and I'm certain they must spend a great deal of time tracking down authentic (and undoubtedly hard to find) spices.

The staff is friendly and almost entirely Indian, meaning they speak English and are focused on ensuring their customers are happy--a commitment which is still too-lacking in many tourist areas in Southeast Asia. Don't be afraid to share your preferences: No heat! A little heat! Heat stolen from Hell itself! 

Mumtaz is located in the backpacker area and its dishes are priced accordingly: a couple of bucks will get you anything on the menu, and the thalis (a complete meal) are a real bargain. The servings are large, enough so that we sometimes bring leftovers home.

I've probably gone on a bit too long here but I want to make clear: Mumtaz is an exceptionally good restaurant, enough to keep locals like myself coming back. If you're in HCMC I suggest you stop by--you won't be disappointed!
